title: Humans tamed the mammoth
premise: Around 12,000 BCE steppe herders coax young woolly mammoths to winter camps with hay and warmth, and the giants stay. Guarded and well fed, mammoths thrive as living plows, wool-bearers and slow companions, teaching humans to build wide gates, broad trails and patient towns. The world that follows farms with giants, travels at a walking pace, and measures wealth in wool and kindness.

chain.event: Steppe herders shelter young mammoths at winter camps and feed them with stored hay.
chain.consequence: Mammoths learn to follow humans and pull sleds, starting year-round herding camps.

chain.event: Herders select the calmest mammoths and weave shed wool into warm cloth.
chain.consequence: Wool flocks give steady fiber and draft power, letting villages grow larger and stay settled.

chain.event: Wide-trail villages link to trade wool, grain and timber by mammoth cart.
chain.consequence: Broad gates and shared grazing commons become standard for towns on trade routes.

chain.event: Herd councils grant mammoths grazing rights and rest days.
chain.consequence: Herd care spreads as a civic duty, keeping mammoth families healthy in warming lands.

chain.event: Mammoth post relays carry goods and letters across long distances.
chain.consequence: Travel and farming use gentle teams, shaping cities with large courtyards and slow streets.

chain.event: Steam mills comb and spin mammoth wool at large scale.
chain.consequence: Mammoth wool becomes everyday cloth, and herd commons grow into modern civic centers by 2026.
